title: Seedling: lightweight feature catalog + experiment onramp (scratch)
content:
Topline: build a minimal "seedling" feature catalog UI + API to let small product teams declare, preview, and experiment with inference features quickly. Focus = low-friction, fast feedback, instrumented by default. Not a full flags system — lean UX for LLM features (prompt templates, response adapters, fallback rules, model variant mappings).

Why: teams keep spinning ad-hoc JSON blobs and ad hoc toggles in repos. We want something between 1) internal engineering feature flags and 2) full enterprise feature gating. Seedling should reduce friction for early experiments and provide telemetry hooks so product owners can measure impact on quality & cost.

Primary user: PM/engineer who wants to try a new response-shaping strategy or fallback policy for a chat product for a week without a big infra change.

Goals (MVP):
- Create / edit small feature definitions via console and API (name, description, scope, artifact references).
- Attach: prompt template, response post-processor snippet (js/py-like DSL), model mapping (eg gpt-4 -> gpt-4o-slim), cost cap per request.
- Quick preview: run a single input through the declared feature in console to see before/after (diff).
- Basic rollout: percentage-based assignment by token or request.
- Telemetry: automatic metrics emitted (requests, avg latency, tokens, quality eval hook).
- One-click revert / archive.

User stories (scratch):
- As a PM I want to create a response filter that trims salutations for mobile UI, test it against sample prompts, and roll out to 5% in 10 minutes.
- As an engineer I want to attach an A/B mapping that routes heavy prompt requests to a quantized variant to reduce cost for low-value flows.
- As an SRE I need the seedling to fail closed (no behavior change) if the runtime integration is unhealthy.

Acceptance criteria (rough):
- Console: create/edit flows with validation; sample preview shows both original and transformed outputs; preview logs tokens & latency.
- API: POST /seedling/features -> returns feature id; PATCH to update rollout.
- Rollouts respect Dedicated/Private model pinning rules (cannot route to hosted-only variants if customer is private).
- Telemetry events show feature_id tag in our tracing and cost dashboards.

Wireframe thoughts (quick):
- Left rail: feature list (status, % rollout, owner). Middle: editor / preview with two panes (input, before/after). Right: telemetry quick glance (tokens, latency, error rate).

Operational constraints / safety:
- Default sandbox: new features start in "preview" mode (console-only) until owner enables rollout.
- Runtime sandboxing: post-processors run inside a tightly sandboxed WASM or restricted eval to avoid data exfil. Need collaboration with security.
- Fallback behavior: if post-processor errors, the request should either (a) return original model output (safe), or (b) route to configured fallback variant. Default = original output + error telemetry.

Metrics to watch (initial):
- Activation rate (how many features created per org per month).
- Preview->Rollout conversion % (are previews converted to rollouts?).
- Impact on tokens/cost and user-facing quality (NPS or evals).
- Percentage of runtime failures from post-processors.

Privacy/compliance note: seedling must respect model privacy tiers. Features that touch PII parsing or structured extraction should be flagged and require explicit approval for Private deployments.

Rollout plan (fast):
- Week 0–2: internal alpha with product + 1 solutions team. Console prototype + API stub + local runtime harness.
- Week 3–5: dogfood on 2 internal products (chat assist, docs summarizer). Add telemetry plumbing.
- Week 6–8: invite 3 external beta customers (early adopters). Add controls for Dedicated/Private.

Open questions / TODOs (my notes):
- DSL choice for post-processor: small JS subset vs WASM vs serverless function. Tradeoffs: ease vs security. Talk to security + infra.
- How to represent feature scope: route-level, user-segment, token-threshold, session-type? Need a compact grammar.
- Rollout semantics: should be sampling by request, by token, or by user? For LLM experiments, token-weighted sampling matters.
- Integration with rollouts page/air traffic controller: should these features appear in existing rollout dashboards? Probably yes. Link to rollout-id.
- Who owns cleanup? Features should have TTL or review reminders so stale experiments don't accumulate. Add archival policy.
- Cost guardrails: per-feature budget enforcement (monthly $ or token cap) — how to enforce across Dedicated?

Quick tasks (next actions):
- Draft API shapes for feature create / update / preview (schema).
- 1-pager for security review focusing on sandboxing choices.
- Mock console screen (Figma quick).
- Pick 2 internal products for dogfood and write short test plan (3–5 sample prompts each).

Related links / inspiration:
- existing rollout UI (console/rollouts) — reuse list view + telemetry sparklines.
- prompt-studio / composer ideas for prompt attachment.

Notes-to-self: keep this intentionally minimal. Main value prop = low friction + instrumented. Avoid building full feature flag semantics (no complex targeting initially). Start with a tight scope and iterate based on conversion metrics.

End of scratch. Keep as a mutable note.
